title: Introduce lean cost bootloader and CPI-aware quant scheduler
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Adds a lightweight tenant bootloader that applies conservative batch/cache defaults and a CPI-aware quant scheduler; opt-in via feature flag; improves unit economics for low-traffic tenants without impacting latency SLOs.
description:
Context and motivation: Many tenants operate at low to moderate QPS where large, aggressive prefill and quant policies either waste GPU cycles or cause brittle regressions when traffic patterns shift. This PR introduces a compact 'lean cost bootloader' that applies conservative batching/caching defaults at tenant onboarding and a CPI-aware quant scheduler that gradually ramps quantization levels in production based on measured cost-per-inference (CPI) and quality signals.

What this PR does (single-string description): Adds a tenant bootloader that populates per-tenant defaults (small continuous-batching window, conservative prefix cache TTLs, disabled aggressive KV prefill) and a runtime scheduler that: (1) observes CPI and latency SLOs, (2) simulates short quantization trials on a small shadow traffic fraction, (3) promotes safe quant profiles when the CPI/quality tradeoff is favorable, and (4) falls back automatically on any regression. The implementation is intentionally small and modular so it can be enabled as an opt-in feature for Dedicated and Private installs.

Key changes:
- runtime/bootloader/lean_bootloader.go: tenant defaults loader and migration hooks to avoid noisy onboarding changes.
- runtime/quant/scheduler.go: CPI-aware quant scheduling state machine and shadow trial harness.
- api/v1/tenant_defaults.go: new endpoints for listing and overriding bootloader defaults.
- cli/costctl/main.go: lightweight CLI to preview, dry-run, and apply bootloader profiles per-tenant.
- configs/default_profiles.yaml: new conservative profiles for batching, cache TTLs, and quant buckets.
- docs/operations/lean-bootloader.md: operator guide and rollback steps.

Checklist (what I validated):
- [x] Unit tests for scheduler state transitions and fallback logic.
- [x] E2E smoke that verifies bootloader does not change defaults for tenants who already customized settings.
- [x] Microbenchmarks: measured CPI delta across three representative low-QPS workloads.
- [x] Integration test: shadow trials run and auto-promote path exercised in CI test harness.
- [x] Docs added for ops and a short CLI usage guide.

Benchmarks (summary):
- Low-QPS text generation workload A (avg 3 qps): baseline CPI $0.038 -> bootloader with conservative quant (int8 hybrid) $0.031 (≈18% cost reduction), p99 latency +1.8% (<SL0 margin of 5%).
- Low-QPS summarization workload B (avg 0.7 qps): baseline CPI $0.061 -> shadow-promoted quant $0.049 (≈20% reduction), no quality regression on canonical eval prompts (BLEU stable within noise).
- Note: we limit shadow trials to <=2% traffic and auto-fallback on a single regression signal to preserve quality.

Configuration & rollout notes:
- Feature flag: runtime.features.lean_cost_bootloader = true (default: false for hosted until we run gradual rollout).
- Tenant-level opt-in: API /v1/tenant/{id}/defaults?source=bootloader allows operators to see proposed changes before apply.
- CLI: costctl preview --tenant TID --dry-run shows proposed batch/cache/quant deltas and estimated CPI improvement.
- Safe defaults: bootloader will not change any tenant that has custom overrides. It only applies to tenants with no explicit batching/cache/quant settings.

Failure modes & rollback:
- If shadow quant trials detect a quality regression above configured thresholds (configurable in configs/default_profiles.yaml), the trial is aborted and the scheduler marks that profile as blacklisted for the tenant for 72h.
- Operators can revert applied profiles via API or costctl rollback --tenant TID --since=<timestamp>.

Testing performed in CI and staging:
- Extended unit and integration test suites added; CI runs a synthetic workload that exercises the scheduler promotion/fallback loop.
- Staging run for two weeks on a subset of Dedicated tenants; no SLO violations observed.

Related work and tradeoffs:
- This is intentionally conservative and complements (rather than replaces) the autoscale-heavy prefills we already use for high-QPS tenants. The bootloader targets cost-savings on the long tail of tenants.
- We avoid aggressive cross-tenant optimization to preserve fairness and isolation.

Docs and migration guide: docs/operations/lean-bootloader.md contains step-by-step enabling instructions and recommended monitoring dashboards (CPI per-tenant, shadow trial success rate, promo rate, fallback count).

Outstanding items / follow-ups (tracked in Linear): ENG-1543: dashboard panels for per-tenant CPI heatmap; ENG-1608: telemetry enrichment for quantized model token-level diffs.
